sentences.text: Heightingtonaspis was a member of the class Placodermi, an ancient group of armored fish.
The type species Heightingtonaspis anglica was originally named Phlyctaenius anglicus by Ramsay Traquair in 1890.
The holotype specimen of Heightingtonaspis anglica was discovered on the surface in Shropshire, England, and dated to 416 million years old.
Heightingtonaspis clarkei was originally named Kujdanowiaspis clarkei by Charles R. Eastman in 1907.
Heightingtonaspis clarkei was reassigned to the genus Heightingtonaspis by Denison in 1978.
Heightingtonaspis willsi was originally named Kujdanowiaspis willsi by White in 1961 and later reassigned to the genus Heightingtonaspis, which was created by White in 1969.
Heightingtonaspis willsi was discovered in Shropshire, England, the same location as Heightingtonaspis anglica.
Heightingtonaspis belongs to the parent group Actinolepididae.
Heightingtonaspis is classified in the family Actinolepididae.
These creatures lived during the Lochkovian stage, between 419.62 and 413.02 million years ago.
Fossils have also been found in the Senni Beds of Wales.
